blocks.html: And do not excuse yourself by my sisters, nor by my Uncle: for there is no father, mother, Uncle, sisters nor brothers who ought better to know their son, nephew or brother than the wife ought to know the husband. And of the disaster which has befallen our house, no one is to blame but you. Whereupon the commissioners tried to excuse the said de Rols: but at this first meeting could never soften his heart, nor turn him from his austerity. Thus the imposture of the said du Tilh being entirely discovered, and the newcomer received and recognised by all as the sole Martin Guerre: and the trial by this means fully instructed so as to be judged definitively, and the same having been reviewed, the Court, upon great and mature deliberation, pronounced the decision which follows.

SEEN the trial conducted by the Judge of Rieux against Arnauld du Tilh, called Pansette, calling himself Martin Guerre, prisoner in the Conciergerie, appellant from the said Judge, etc. It has been declared that the Court has set aside and sets aside the appeal of the said du Tilh, and the judgment appealed from, as null. And for the punishment and reparation of the imposture, forgery, substitution of name and person, adultery, rape, sacrilege, enslavement, theft and other offences committed by the said du Tilh, prisoner, resulting from the said trial, the Court has condemned and condemns him to make public penance (amende honorable) before the Church of the place of Artigat, and there, on his knees, in a shirt, bareheaded and barefoot, having the halter round his neck and holding in his hands a burning wax taper, to ask pardon of God, of the King, of Justice, and of the said Martin Guerre and de Rols, married persons: and this done, the said du Tilh shall be delivered into the hands of the executioner, who shall make him go the rounds through the accustomed streets and crossroads of the said place of Artigat: and, the halter round his neck, shall lead him before the house of the said Martin Guerre, there to be hanged and strangled on a gallows which shall be erected there for that purpose, and afterwards his body burnt. And for certain causes and considerations moving the Court thereto, it has adjudged and adjudges the goods of the said du Tilh to the daughter procreated by his doings and of the said de Rols, under pretext of the marriage by him falsely pretended, substituting the name and person of the said Martin Guerre and by this means deceiving the said de Rols — the costs of Justice deducted. And moreover, it has dismissed and dismisses from the case and suit the said Martin Guerre and Bertrande de Rols, together with the said Pierre Guerre, uncle of the said Martin: and has remanded and remands the same du Tilh to the said Judge of Rieux, to have this present decision put into execution according to its form and tenor.
Pronounced judicially, the twelfth day of September, 1560.
